attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira is in disguise; Virata is the king of the Matsya kingdom

extraction_text: King Virata observes Yudhishthira's majestic appearance and questions his assembly about the stranger's identity.

attributes.relationships: Virata is suspicious but impressed by Yudhishthira's regal bearing

extraction_text: Yudhishthira approaches King Virata and introduces himself as a Brahmin named Kanka who has lost everything and seeks refuge.

attributes.action: False introduction and request for refuge
attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira presents himself as a dependent; Virata is the potential protector

extraction_text: Yudhishthira claims to be a Brahmin from the tiger-step family, a friend of Yudhishthira, a gambler skilled in dice, and known by the name Kanka.

attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira maintains his disguise as Kanka

extraction_text: King Virata offers Yudhishthira rulership over the Matsya people, declaring himself as Yudhishthira's servant and expressing fondness for clever gamblers.

attributes.relationships: Virata elevates Yudhishthira's status to co-ruler; relationship becomes one of mutual service

extraction_text: Yudhishthira requests the favor that in any major dispute, he will not suffer loss, and those he defeats will lose their wealth.

attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira secures advantageous terms under his disguise

extraction_text: King Virata grants Yudhishthira's request, promises protection, declares him co-ruler of the land, and offers shared privileges.

attributes.relationships: Virata formally establishes Yudhishthira as an equal ruler and protector

extraction_text: Yudhishthira settles in Virata's kingdom, living there respected and happy, with his true identity remaining unknown.

attributes.relationships: Yudhishthira successfully integrates into Virata's court under his disguise

extraction_text: A strong, terrifying, and radiant man with a lion-like gait approached King Virata, dressed as a cook and holding kitchen utensils and a blue-bladed knife.

attributes.description: Bhima disguises himself and approaches King Virata's court.

extraction_text: King Virata, upon seeing Bhima, signaled him to stop and expressed astonishment to the assembly, questioning who this extraordinary man was and admitting he could not discern his thoughts.

attributes.description: King Virata is impressed by Bhima's appearance and seeks to identify him.

extraction_text: Bhima approached King Virata and introduced himself as the cook Ballava, offering his culinary services to the king.

attributes.description: Bhima presents his false identity and seeks employment as a cook.

extraction_text: King Virata expressed disbelief that Bhima was a cook, noting his divine appearance, auspiciousness, beauty, and courage, and comparing him to the thousand-eyed god Indra.

attributes.description: King Virata doubts Bhima's claimed profession due to his majestic demeanor.

extraction_text: Bhima insisted he was a cook and servant, claiming expertise in unique dishes previously tasted by King Yudhishthira, and boasted of his strength in wrestling and combat with elephants and lions.

attributes.description: Bhima reinforces his disguise by detailing his culinary and physical prowess.

extraction_text: King Virata granted Bhima the favor of working in the kitchen, appointing him as the chief cook and supervisor of all kitchen staff, though he believed Bhima deserved to rule the world.

attributes.description: King Virata employs Bhima as head cook, acknowledging his apparent greatness.

extraction_text: Bhima was settled in the kitchen, highly favored by King Virata, and lived there with his true identity unknown to anyone, including servants.

attributes.description: Bhima successfully hides his identity while serving in King Virata's kitchen.
